profile: shared behavioral scenarios; Linux low-level bindings and qualified public SDK adapters

steps: Install public SDK, examples and native artifacts in a clean consumer outside the checkout
Fail persistence, native-response allocation and confirmation hooks for every mutation purpose
Stop without rerunning the handler and recover exact accepted bytes after host/node/store loss
Resume the requester from durable waiting state and verify its full-width reply
Read bounded Table pages and retained points, then consume original complete-result IPC after runner disposal
Revoke access during result reading and preserve retirement/read/ownership errors
scenarios.limits: Python 3.13 public runner and clean Linux Nix-linked wheels; one worker, serialized synchronous handlers, bounded native I/O and query workspace. Other language adapters must add equivalent observations. Optional PyArrow 23 consumes owned segments separately.

steps: Require explicit query opt-in and start a typed native plan from an authenticated call
Persist every control/capture/receive proposal before dispatch
Lose an accepted staging response and retry the exact signed bytes
Restart both workers, authority and disk provider after a segment seal
Verify complete provenance and decode copied IPC after native disposal
Read the same result through the native port and reject stale scope and revoked access
scenarios.limits: Explicit growing C/port handles on disk Ursula with 64 resident pages, one 1 MiB workspace per query-enabled handle and 8192-byte segment bounds. Public SDK runners and optional Arrow adapters have separate qualification.

steps: Probe native operation support and prepare explicit v3 operations
Admit a full-width principal's request and lose the response
Restart the node/provider and retry opaque bytes from a fresh host without its seed
Reject malformed read/receipt responses without inventing a mutation rejection
Revoke access before both reads and historical receipt recovery
scenarios.limits: Qualifies the explicit raw ABI and shared signature/operation fixtures, not a public SDK handler runner or a growing Station foreign ABI.

steps: Admit an input without running its handler
Commit state and a reply intent
Deliver the reply
Consume the reply in its destination
Race independent handles with different bodies at the same principal sequence
Retry each exact request from the other handle
Race identical requests at the next sequence
Inspect mailbox progress without running a handler
Persist a frozen signed request before submission
Lose the response after acceptance
Destroy the native operation
Import in a fresh host without the signing seed
Recover the original receipt with byte-identical retry
Commit a durable wait and finish the caller turn
Exit the caller host
Capture a reply and exit the service host
Publish from a new service host
Resume the caller through its recorded correlation and complete the result
Admit a malformed framework envelope
Poll until the declared decode-failure policy blocks the input
Poll again without dispatching a handler
Inspect the same unconsumed input and unchanged state
Hold a native request in flight
Cancel only its host await
Dispose the handle while native work is owned
Keep the event loop responsive until cleanup joins
Reject use of the disposed handle
scenarios.limits: The stalled transport does not establish a durable outcome; cancellation of a local await does not cancel authority work. Exact accepted-response loss is covered separately.

steps: Report one accepted receipt through the real native response path
Fail each response allocation in turn
Require uncertainty on failure and release all owned buffers
Verify the transport submitted exactly once

proofs.anchor: test "every post-commit response allocation failure remains uncertain and releases buffers"

scenarios.limits: Native allocation enumeration uses an injected accepted transport; disk/HTTP and host schedulers have separate proofs.
